bugs.description: Sign of daysBack flipped: startOfDayMs now adds daysBack instead of subtracting it, so 'N days back' walks into the future instead of the past. Corrupts every caller that reconstructs a day boundary (readTrailHistory, etc.).
Speed-based segment-cut threshold raised 10x (40 -> 400), silently disabling the GPS-teleport/speed-jump detection that is supposed to split a trail into separate segments.
Round-trip mileage is no longer doubled (roundTrip = miles instead of miles * 2), so pay-per-mile is overestimated by roughly 2x and offers are misclassified as better pay than they actually are.
speechRecognizer is nulled out without calling destroy() first, leaking the underlying SpeechRecognizer system resource/mic binding every time the Activity is destroyed.

Result of Location.distanceBetween (already meters) is divided by 1000 as if converting to kilometers, but the function is named/used as distanceMeters everywhere (segment cut thresholds, trimStationaryEnds drift thresholds), so every downstream distance comparison is now ~1000x too small.

OfferQueue (a singleton object) now stores the raw Context passed into enqueue() instead of context.applicationContext. If an Activity context is ever passed in, the Activity can never be garbage-collected, a classic static-reference memory leak.

Comparison operator flipped (< became >): cleanup now deletes every trail file newer than the cutoff date (the recent data worth keeping) while leaving everything older than keepDays untouched -- the exact opposite of the intended retention policy.
Earth-radius constant swapped from miles (3958.8) to kilometers (6371.0) inside the haversine helper. Every distance the AI agent context reports as 'mi' is actually ~1.6x too large.

Per-item penalty multiplier inflated 10x (0.05 -> 0.5) in scoreOffer. Offers with >5 items are penalized ~10x too heavily on pay-per-mile, so good multi-item offers get mislabeled as 'low pay'/'very low pay'.

Default removed from scoreOffer's itemCount parameter (Int? = null -> Int?). scoreOffer is still called with two args elsewhere (RouteFitAccessibilityService.scoreOffer(amount, platformMiles)), so that call site no longer compiles -- a cross-file contract break invisible from this file's diff alone.

findings.issue: daysBack sign flipped: add(Calendar.DAY_OF_YEAR, daysBack) adds future days instead of subtracting past days, breaking all historical range queries.
Speed outlier threshold raised from 40.0 to 400.0 m/s (or mph). At 400 m/s nearly all erroneous GPS jumps will pass the filter, corrupting trip distance calculations.
distanceMeters now divides by 1000, returning km not meters. Any caller expecting meters (e.g. the 500.0 m cut threshold above) will be off by 1000x.
File deletion condition inverted: dayStr > cutoffDay deletes newer files and keeps old ones, the opposite of the intended cleanup behavior.
appContext now stores the Activity/Service context instead of applicationContext. This leaks the caller context for the lifetime of the singleton OfferQueue object.
Earth radius changed from 3958.8 (miles) to 6371.0 (km). Fix is correct if callers expect km; must be consistent with all call sites.
speechRecognizer?.destroy() removed in onDestroy. The recognizer object is nulled but never destroyed, leaking the underlying resource and potentially causing ANRs.
roundTrip changed from miles*2 to miles (one-way only), and itemPenalty multiplier increased 10x (0.05 to 0.5). Scoring semantics silently changed; heavy multi-item orders may score negative.
itemCount default value removed, making the parameter mandatory. Any existing call sites that omit itemCount will now fail to compile.

findings.issue: Earth radius changed from miles (3958.8) to km (6371.0) without updating result unit handling. All distance calculations expecting miles will now return km.
startOfDayMs changed from subtracting daysBack to adding it, which will return a date in the future instead of the past.
Trail file deletion condition flipped from dayStr < cutoffDay to dayStr > cutoffDay. This could delete recent files instead of old ones.
Speed cutoff increased from 40.0 to 400.0 units, likely km/h or mph. This may allow unrealistic speeds through the filter.
distanceMeters now returns distance in kilometers instead of meters (divided by 1000). All callers must expect km.
roundTrip changed from miles*2 to just miles, halving the distance used in scoring. This will make offers appear more profitable.
Item penalty multiplier increased from 0.05 to 0.5, making the penalty 10x stronger. This will significantly penalize large orders.
Removed speechRecognizer?.destroy() call; this may leave a native resource leak if the recognizer is not cleaned up elsewhere.
ItemCount parameter changed from nullable with default null to required nullable. All callers must now provide this argument explicitly.
Storing Activity context instead of applicationContext may leak the Activity if the context is held beyond its lifecycle.

findings.issue: Storing a direct context reference in a singleton object introduces a memory leak.
The logic for calculating a past date is inverted. `add(..., daysBack)` will move the date into the future if `daysBack` is positive.
The file cleanup logic is inverted. It now compares `dayStr > cutoffDay`, which would delete recent files instead of old ones.
The speed check threshold was increased from 40.0 m/s to 400.0 m/s (over 890 mph), which makes the check ineffective for any realistic scenario.
The call to `speechRecognizer?.destroy()` was removed from `onDestroy`, which will cause a resource leak.
The function `distanceMeters` is now dividing by 1000, causing it to return kilometers instead of meters, which contradicts its name.
The variable `roundTrip` is now assigned the one-way distance, making its name misleading and the code harder to understand.
The Earth's radius constant `R` was changed from miles (3958.8) to kilometers (6371.0), changing the distance calculation's unit.
